3	SYNTHETIC EVALUATION MATERIAL. This is the entire fictional source package. Source language: English. No external facts or quotations may be added.

5	## Brief
6	
7	Write a journalistic customer case for operations managers at small housing companies. The publisher is the supplier, Svale Systems. The customer, Elm Quay Housing, should remain the acting party. Approximately 400 words, as material allows. Markdown. No author name supplied. The optional next step is the supplied implementation checklist at https://example.invalid/svale/checklist; it is a document to read, not a consultation booking or a product trial.
8	
9	## Material
10	
11	Elm Quay Housing manages 640 flats. In September 2025 its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings. Previously telephone reports and emails were stored separately. The team wanted staff on different shifts to see the same information. It chose Svale Systems after testing whether the log could show the status of each repair. No comparison with another supplier is available.
12	
13	The maintenance team designed its categories and kept telephone reporting open for residents. Svale configured the log and trained six staff during two sessions. The trial lasted eight weeks. Elm Quay's internal trial note, 4 December 2025, says that 31 repair reports were entered. It excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial. Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial and three in the preceding eight-week period. The periods had different workloads, and the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software. There are no cost, resident-satisfaction or completion-time measurements.
14	
15	Customer interview with maintenance supervisor Maya Lind, complete usable quotations:
16	
17	- “We wanted the evening shift to see what the morning shift had already done. The categories were ours; Svale helped us put them into the log.”
18	- “We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports. I would set that time aside before the next building starts.”
19	- “I would choose to do the trial again. Having one view of the reports helps us, but I would leave an extra week for preparation.”
20	
21	Lind did not recommend Svale to every housing company. Her final quotation is her actual, qualified assessment. It is not an inference from the figures. The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs. The supplier approved publication of this case as supplier-published material; it is not independent journalism. All interviews occurred by email, and no physical scene, emotion or remembered dialogue is provided. Translation of the quotations is permitted, preserving stance and qualification.
22	
23	## Forbidden inferences / judging

1	# Quoting speech
2	
3	Read this before putting quotation marks around anything somebody said. It applies to interview transcripts, recorded remarks, meeting notes, and any other material where the words are a person's rather than a document's.
4	
5	Speech is not written prose, and a transcript quoted raw reads as carelessness towards the speaker rather than fidelity to them. So a spoken quotation may be repaired — cautiously, within a boundary that is easier to state than to feel your way to.
6	
7	When translating permitted quotations, preserve meaning, stance, certainty and distinctive voice in idiomatic target-language speech, not source-language syntax. The restrictions below protect that substance; they do not require word-for-word translation. Make an implicit referent explicit only when the supplied context settles it. Where the meaning remains ambiguous, paraphrase what is established rather than inventing a fluent interpretation.
8	
9	## What may be repaired
10	
11	The syntax of speech: a sentence abandoned halfway and restarted, a subject left behind by its verb, a clause that never closes. Fillers — *you know*, *sort of*, *liksom*, *alltså* — where they carry nothing. Repetition that is the speaker searching for a word rather than insisting on one. False starts, and the small disfluencies a person does not hear themselves make.
12	
13	That is the whole list. Everything on it is noise the speaker did not intend to produce, and removing it leaves what they meant to say.
14	
15	## What may not
16	
17	**Meaning.** Not narrowed, not widened, not sharpened. A speaker who said *most of them* has not said *all of them*, and one who said *we looked at it* has not said *we rejected it*.
18	
19	**Stance.** Approval stays approval, reluctance stays reluctance, and a speaker who was careful not to blame anybody is not made to blame somebody by a tidier sentence.
20	
21	**Certainty.** *I think*, *probably*, *as far as I know*, and *we are not sure yet* are the claim, not padding on it. Removing a hedge manufactures a confidence the speaker did not have; adding one takes away a confidence they did.
22	
23	**Distinctive wording.** Where the speaker reached for an unusual word, an image, a piece of slang, or a phrasing that is theirs, it stays. Smoothing it into the register of the surrounding article is the most tempting of these failures and the one a reader can least detect.
24	
25	**A self-correction.** Where a speaker gives a number or a fact and then corrects it, the correction is what they said. Quoting the first version is a misquotation; quoting a version that never existed — the correction with the correcting away — is worse.
26	
27	**Anything additive.** Add no new meaning: no fact, stance, certainty, name, figure or connection that the speaker did not supply. A permitted repair or translation may change words only to render that same meaning.
28	
29	## When to paraphrase instead
30	
31	Where fidelity is uncertain, paraphrase. A paraphrase that attributes carefully — *she said the change had taken about a year, and that she was not sure it would hold* — is accurate, useful, and honest about what the material supports. A fluent direct quotation assembled out of a fragmentary answer is none of those things, however good it sounds.
32	
33	The cases that should turn into paraphrase: material that is a summary of what somebody said rather than their words; a transcript too broken to repair inside the boundary above; several remarks that would have to be welded together to make one sentence; and any moment where you find yourself choosing between two readings of what the speaker meant.
34	
35	Signal what the material actually is. Where the source is notes rather than a recording, the text says what the person said and does not pretend to their exact wording.
36	
37	## What stays outside this
38	
39	Whether the speaker approves the quotation. Quote approval is a human arrangement between the writer and the person quoted, and nothing here verifies it or stands in for it. A draft may say a quotation is unapproved; it may not treat the absence of approval as a problem it has solved.

# Source-comparison report 1: Elm Quay draft (sv) against source package (en)

## A. Claim accounting

Each item gives the draft passage (D), the source passage (S) in the source's own words, and what differs.

1. **Title.** D: "Elm Quay provade gemensam reparationslogg i två hus". S: "its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings." Differences: the company stands in for its own maintenance team. The team belongs to Elm Quay, so the actor is the same. No finding.

2. **Lead, sentence 1.** D: "Efter åtta veckors försök med en reparationslogg från Svale Systems skulle arbetsledaren för underhållet på bostadsbolaget Elm Quay Housing göra om det – men med en extra vecka för förberedelser." S: "The trial lasted eight weeks." / "maintenance supervisor Maya Lind" / "I would choose to do the trial again. [...] but I would leave an extra week for preparation." The conditional modality ("skulle", "would") and the reservation (the extra week) are both kept. "Efter" states only the sequence. No finding.

3. **Lead, sentence 2.** D: "Här är vad teamet gjorde, vad siffrorna visar och vad de inte visar." This is an editorial transition, with "de" as plural pronoun referring to "siffrorna". No finding.

4. D: "Elm Quay Housing förvaltar 640 lägenheter." S: "Elm Quay Housing manages 640 flats." No finding.

5. D: "Tidigare förvarades felanmälningar som kom in per telefon och mejl var för sig." S: "Previously telephone reports and emails were stored separately." Difference: the source says "emails", while the draft says fault reports that arrived by email. **Finding F4.**

6. D: "I september 2025 beslutade bolagets eget underhållsteam att pröva en gemensam logg i två av husen." S: "In September 2025 its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings." Time, actor, modality ("decided") and scope all match. "två av husen" presupposes that Elm Quay has further buildings. Lind's quotation settles that: "before the next building starts", and "The trial has not yet expanded". No finding.

7. D: "Arbetsledaren Maya Lind berättar hur teamet lade upp arbetet och vad hon skulle ändra på inför nästa hus." S: the three quotations, including "I would set that time aside before the next building starts" and "I would leave an extra week for preparation". **Pronoun "hon":** third person, singular, natural gender feminine. Support: the source refers to Lind as "Her final quotation is her actual, qualified assessment." No finding.

8. **H2.** D: "Teamet prövade loggen, Svale satte upp den". S: "its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log" / "Svale configured the log". "den" is grammatical gender only (loggen). No finding.

9. D: "Innan valet föll på Svale Systems undersökte underhållsteamet om loggen kunde visa var varje reparation stod." S: "It chose Svale Systems after testing whether the log could show the status of each repair." Difference: the source says "testing", while the draft says "undersökte" (investigated or examined). **Finding F5.**

10. D: "Något underlag som jämför Svale med andra leverantörer finns inte." S: "No comparison with another supplier is available." Difference: the source says "not available", while the draft says the comparison does not exist. **Finding F1.**

11. D: "Svale konfigurerade loggen och utbildade sex medarbetare vid två tillfällen." S: "Svale configured the log and trained six staff during two sessions." No finding.

12. D: "Teamet höll telefonanmälan öppen för de boende." S: "The maintenance team designed its categories and kept telephone reporting open for residents." No finding. The team's own design of the categories is carried by quotation 1.

13. D: "Vad teamet ville uppnå förklarar Maya Lind i en mejlintervju:" S: "The team wanted staff on different shifts to see the same information." / "All interviews occurred by email". No finding.

14. **Quotation 1.** D: "– Vi ville att kvällsskiftet skulle se vad morgonskiftet redan hade gjort. Kategorierna var våra; Svale hjälpte oss att lägga in dem i loggen." S: "We wanted the evening shift to see what the morning shift had already done. The categories were ours; Svale helped us put them into the log." Person and number match: "vi"/"oss" corresponds to "we"/"us", first person plural. "dem" is plural and refers to the categories. Meaning and stance match. See Section C.

15. **H2.** D: "Anteckningen kopplar inte siffrorna till loggen". S: "the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software." / "Elm Quay's internal trial note [...] says that 31 repair reports were entered." Differences: "the difference" becomes all the figures, and "attribute" becomes "link" (koppla). **Finding F2.**

16. D: "Enligt Elm Quays interna anteckning om försöket, daterad den 4 december 2025, fördes 31 felanmälningar in under de åtta veckorna." S: "Elm Quay's internal trial note, 4 December 2025, says that 31 repair reports were entered." Difference: the draft adds the time frame "under de åtta veckorna". **Finding F3.** The attribution to the note is kept.

17. D: "Anteckningen räknar inte med akuta ärenden eller arbete som beställdes före försöket." S: "It excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial." The exclusion keeps the source's scope, attached to the note. No finding.

18. D: "Mediantiden från anmälan till att ärendet fördelades var två arbetsdagar under försöket, mot tre under de åtta veckorna dessförinnan." S: "Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial and three in the preceding eight-week period." "fördelades" is the established Swedish term for handing a case to a technician, and nothing in the material separates it from "assignment". The unit (working days), the statistic (median) and both periods match. No finding.

19. D: "Arbetsbelastningen skilde sig mellan perioderna, och anteckningen tillskriver uttryckligen inte skillnaden programvaran." S: "The periods had different workloads, and the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software." No finding.

20. D: "Siffran gäller tiden till fördelning, inte tiden tills reparationen var klar." S: "Median time from report to assignment" / "There are no [...] completion-time measurements." / "Do not turn assignment time into completion time." Supported. No finding.

21. D: "Det finns inga mätningar av kostnader, de boendes nöjdhet eller tid till avslutat arbete." S: "There are no cost, resident-satisfaction or completion-time measurements." Same modality as the source. No finding.

22. **H2.** D: "Maya Lind ser tillbaka på försöket". This is an editorial heading resting on the quotations. No finding.

23. **Quotation 2.** D: "– Vi lade mer tid på att enas om kategorierna än på att föra in de första anmälningarna. Den tiden skulle jag avsätta innan nästa hus kommer i gång, skriver Maya Lind." S: "We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports. I would set that time aside before the next building starts." "skriver" fits "All interviews occurred by email". Person and number match ("vi", "jag"). See Section C.

24. D: "Försöket som helhet bedömer hon så här:" S: "Her final quotation is her actual, qualified assessment." "hon" is third person, singular and feminine, supported by "Her". "som helhet" is defensible because the quotation evaluates the trial and whether to repeat it. No finding.

25. **Quotation 3.** D: "– Jag skulle välja att göra försöket igen. Att ha en samlad bild av anmälningarna hjälper oss, men jag skulle ge förberedelserna en vecka till." S: "I would choose to do the trial again. Having one view of the reports helps us, but I would leave an extra week for preparation." Stance, conditional modality and qualification are kept. See Section C.

26. **H2.** D: "Kategorierna ska prövas på större reparationer först". S: "the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs." "prövas" corresponds to checking how the categories work, and "först" corresponds to before the decision. Defensible. No finding.

27. D: "Försöket har ännu inte utvidgats. Teamet beslutar om nästa steg när det har sett hur kategorierna fungerar för större reparationer." S: "The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs." "det" is grammatical neuter only (teamet), with no natural gender. No finding.

28. D: "Någon rekommendation av Svale till alla bostadsbolag gav Maya Lind inte." S: "Lind did not recommend Svale to every housing company." The scope matches and the customer's reservation survives. No finding.

29. D: "Leder du driften på ett mindre bostadsbolag och funderar på ett liknande försök kan du läsa [en checklista för införande](https://example.invalid/svale/checklist)." S: "The optional next step is the supplied implementation checklist [...]; it is a document to read, not a consultation booking or a product trial." The destination is described accurately. "du" addresses the reader and makes no claim. No finding.

30. D: "Texten är en kundberättelse som Svale Systems publicerar och är inte oberoende journalistik." S: "The publisher is the supplier, Svale Systems." / "supplier-published material; it is not independent journalism." No finding.

31. **Byline** "Av Thomas Barregren": per instruction, this comes from the invocation. No finding.

## B. Source-support findings

**F1: "finns inte" turns "not available" into non-existence (paragraph under the first H2).**
- Draft: "Något underlag som jämför Svale med andra leverantörer finns inte."
- Source: "No comparison with another supplier is available."
- Problem: the source reports the state of the material, while the draft asserts that no such comparison exists.
- Case where the source holds and the draft fails: the team did compare Svale with another supplier, but that comparison was not supplied. No supplied statement excludes this.
- Repair: "Någon jämförelse med andra leverantörer finns inte tillgänglig."

**F2: The heading widens the note's non-attribution (H2 "Anteckningen kopplar inte siffrorna till loggen").**
- Source: "the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software."
- Problem: the source withholds causal attribution for one thing, the difference in median assignment time. The heading instead says the note does not connect *the figures* to *the log* at all.
- Case where the source holds and the draft fails: the note counts "31 repair reports [...] entered", which are entries in the log itself, and it could take the medians from log timestamps. The note would then link the figures to the log while still not attributing the difference to the software. Nothing in the material excludes this. The count of entries is by its nature a log figure.
- Repair: "Anteckningen tillskriver inte programvaran skillnaden".

**F3: Added time frame for the 31 entries.**
- Draft: "fördes 31 felanmälningar in under de åtta veckorna."
- Source: "Elm Quay's internal trial note, 4 December 2025, says that 31 repair reports were entered."
- Problem: the source gives no period for the count. The draft limits it to the eight trial weeks.
- Case where the source holds and the draft fails: the eight-week trial ended in late November, and the note dated 4 December counts reports entered up to that date, including some after the trial ended. No supplied statement excludes this.
- Repair: "fördes 31 felanmälningar in." Delete "under de åtta veckorna".

**F4: "emails" narrowed to fault reports by email.**
- Draft: "Tidigare förvarades felanmälningar som kom in per telefon och mejl var för sig."
- Source: "Previously telephone reports and emails were stored separately."
- Problem: the draft asserts that fault reports arrived by email. The source says only that emails were stored separately from telephone reports.
- Case where the source holds and the draft fails: the separately stored emails were correspondence with contractors or colleagues about repairs, not reports from residents. Nothing excludes this.
- Repair: "Tidigare förvarades telefonanmälningar och mejl var för sig."

**F5: "testing" weakened to "undersökte".**
- Draft: "Innan valet föll på Svale Systems undersökte underhållsteamet om loggen kunde visa var varje reparation stod."
- Source: "It chose Svale Systems after testing whether the log could show the status of each repair."
- Problem: "undersöka" also covers reading documentation or asking the vendor. The source states a test.
- Case where the draft holds and the source fails: the team checked the feature only in Svale's product description.
- Repair: "... testade underhållsteamet om loggen kunde visa var varje reparation stod." This is a minor finding.

## C. Translation findings (quotations)

- **Quotation 1:** meaning, stance and the division of roles ("Kategorierna var våra; Svale hjälpte oss ...") are kept. The Swedish is idiomatic and uses a speech dash. No concrete obstruction, so no finding.
- **Quotation 2:** meaning and the conditional ("skulle jag avsätta") are kept. "innan nästa hus kommer i gång" copies the source's own metonymy ("before the next building starts"). It reads naturally in context. No finding.
- **Quotation 3:** the stance ("skulle välja att göra försöket igen"), the qualification ("men jag skulle ge förberedelserna en vecka till") and the modest claim ("hjälper oss") are kept. "en samlad bild av anmälningarna" renders "one view of the reports" as a consolidated overview. Nothing in the context separates the two, and the Swedish is idiomatic. No finding.

No translation findings.

## D. Completion status

Complete. Every factual and attributed claim in the title, lead, headings, body, quotations, link text and disclosure is accounted for. There are five unresolved source-support findings: F1, F2, F3, F4 and F5, with F4 and F5 minor. There are no translation findings.
